test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The accuracy of the dial bore gauge instrument depends on which of the following parts?

options.text: A dot indicator on a linear scale
A marking on a logarithmic dial
A pointer on a graduated dial
An arrow on a semi-circular scale

solution:
The correct answer is __A pointer on a graduated dial**(Option 3)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• A pointer on a graduated dial__ is crucial for the accuracy of a dial bore gauge.
 
• This pointer indicates the measurement reading on the instrument.
 
• The graduated dial provides precise divisions that enhance measurement accuracy.
 
• The combination of a pointer and graduated dial ensures reliable and repeatable measurements.
 
• Proper alignment and calibration of the pointer are essential for maintaining accuracy.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **A dot indicator on a linear scale:**

 
 
• This is not typically used in dial bore gauges as they rely on circular dials.
 
 
 
• **A marking on a logarithmic dial:**
 
 
• This type of marking is not suitable for the precise measurements required by dial bore gauges.
 
 
 
• **An arrow on a semi-circular scale:**
 
 
• Semi-circular scales are less common in dial bore gauges due to limited readability.
